summary: This Dockerfile snippet sets up a Node.js 21 Alpine Linux base image and configures it for cleaner logging and modern package management. It disables colored output from yarn to make logs more readable in CI/CD environments, and enables corepack so the image can use yarn or npm without pre-installing them.

explanations.1: Alpine is a minimal Linux distribution that keeps Docker images small; Node.js 21 is the specific version we want pre-installed in our image.
explanations.4: FORCE_COLOR=0 tells yarn and npm to not add colorful ANSI codes to their output, which makes logs cleaner when read by tools or stored in files.
explanations.7: Corepack is a Node.js tool that manages package managers (yarn, npm, pnpm) for you, so different projects can use different versions without manual installation.
